## Summary

Ensure the herdr audit-freshness predicate enforces the canonical "at-or-near"
semantics and is the **single source of truth** shared by both the icon display
and the downtime (audit-dispatch) worker.

Audit freshness currently lives only in `isAuditFresh()` in
`packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`. It is the basis for the icon display
(`auditIcon` in `icons.ts`) AND is the documented freshness gate reused by the
downtime dispatch audit tier (`selectAuditCandidate` /
`getNextAuditCandidate` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, which
treats `!isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` as "needs a fresh `/skill:audit`").

Running an audit itself bumps the work item's `updatedAt` to within a fraction
of a second of its `auditedAt` (`wl audit-set` + `wl update --audit-text` +
the verdict-driven status transition). A freshness rule that requires a strict
gap on one side (e.g. only `auditedAt` comfortably ahead of `updatedAt`) can
therefore disagree with the just-persisted state. The canonical fix in
SorraAgents (SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4) treats an audit as fresh when its
`auditedAt` is **at or near** the item's `updatedAt` (within a small
tolerance) because a near-simultaneous `updatedAt` bump is the audit's own
persistence write.

This item makes ContextHub's herdr audit-freshness logic follow the same
at-or-near rule so the icon display and the downtime dispatcher agree, and
never disagree on a just-persisted audit.

## Expected behaviour

- `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` returns true (fresh) when `auditedAt`
  is at-or-near `updatedAt` within a small, named tolerance (the audit's own
  persistence write), and false otherwise.
- The icon (`auditIcon` in `icons.ts`) shows the fresh icon for a
  just-persisted audit (no longer shows the stale glyph for an audit the run
  just persisted).
- The downtime audit candidate selection (`selectAuditCandidate` /
  `getNextAuditCandidate` in `downtime-worker.ts`) uses the SAME
  `isAuditFresh` predicate, so a just-persisted fresh audit is NOT a dispatch
  candidate (no redundant `/skill:audit` re-run).
- Only one freshness definition exists; neither consumer re-implements its
  own comparison.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `isAuditFresh` in `icons.ts` treats `auditedAt` at-or-near `updatedAt`
   (within a documented tolerance constant) as fresh, covering the
   audit-persistence case (`auditedAt ~ updatedAt`, delta well under the
   tolerance).
2. A unit test asserts `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` is true for a
   just-persisted audit (auditedAt and updatedAt differ by milliseconds).
3. A unit test asserts a genuinely stale audit (item updated well after the
   audit) is still false (stale), unchanged.
4. `selectAuditCandidate` / `getNextAuditCandidate` in `downtime-worker.ts`
   continue to use the imported `isAuditFresh` as the sole filter; a
   just-persisted fresh item is excluded from candidates.
5. Both consumers import the same helper; no competing freshness comparison
   is introduced in the dispatch or icon paths.

## Notes / Open questions

- `isAuditFresh` currently hard-codes a magic `60000` ms literal. Prefer
  naming a constant (e.g. `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS`) and routing
  both consumers through it.
- Reconcile the comparison shape of `isAuditFresh` (`auditTime > updateTime -
  buffer`) with the canonical at-or-near semantics from the SorraAgents fix so
  both projects express the same intent. Confirm the target semantics with the
  operator before implementing.

## References

- discovered-from: SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4 (SorraAgents audit_runner child
  freshness at-or-near fix) — canonical reference implementation.
- related-to: WL-0MSI9FK2Q0074C31 (Audit candidate selection),
  WL-0MSI9WPNI0044R (Audit dispatch tier), parent WL-0MSI8H3HP700K0RG.
data.title: Unify audit-freshness at-or-near logic across icon display and downtime dispatcher

Mechanism under investigation: wl update --needs-producer-review bumps updatedAt (packages/shared/src/database.ts update()); herdr's isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt) (packages/herdr/src/icons.ts) then reports stale, which (a) degrades the TUI audit icon and (b) re-selects the item for audit-tier dispatch (selectAuditCandidate, packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts).

# Prevent top line info bar from scrolling off screen (WL-0MSNI6TQ5003JY1Z)

## Headline

Fix the Herdr plugin's top `Work Items` info bar wrapping off screen in narrow panes by truncating the header to the terminal width so it never exceeds one row.

## Problem statement

In the Herdr `worklog-selection-list` plugin's list mode, the top info bar (row 0: `Work Items — N item(s) [auto-refresh on] [Downtime Off]` plus optional `(filtered: …)`, `(top …)`, `[paused — hidden]` and code-freeze banners) can exceed the pane width in narrow terminals. The header is assembled by string concatenation without truncation, so when its visible length exceeds `cols` the terminal wraps it onto extra physical rows. When total rendered output then exceeds the `rows - 1` line-count invariant (WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO), the terminal scrolls the first line off the top of the pane and the header is not visible — even with the minimal `[Downtime Off]` status and no idle timestamp.

## Users

- **Herdr worklist users** browsing the selection list in narrow panes (e.g. 80 cols or less, `herdr pane layout` narrow split), who rely on the top bar to see the item count, active filter, auto-refresh and downtime state.

### Example User Stories

- As a Herdr user with a narrow pane and many items, I want the top `Work Items` info bar to stay visible at row 0 regardless of pane width or list content, so I don't lose the item count and system status.
- As a Herdr user, I want a long header (filter + auto-refresh + downtime) to be truncated with an ellipsis rather than wrapping onto a second row and pushing the header off screen.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Header never wraps / always visible at row 0:** In list mode, the header line is truncated to fit the terminal width (visible length ≤ `cols`, ANSI preserved via `truncateLine`) so it occupies exactly one output row. For any `cols` ≥ 40 and any combination of `filterLabel`, `totalCount` (`top N of M`), `autoRefresh`, `panePaused`, and `downtimeStatus` (`[Downtime Off]`, `[Downtime Off (restored)]`, `[downtime paused]`, `[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]`, `[downtime busy]`, `[⏳ downtime dispatching]`), `renderer(…)` output satisfies `stripAnsi(output.split('
')[0]).includes('Work Items')` and `stripAnsi(output.split('
')[0]).length <= cols`.

2. **Line-count invariant holds in narrow panes:** In list mode the full renderer output contains at most `rows - 1` newline-separated lines for any `TermSize` (e.g. 40×24, 80×24, 120×53, 60×20) and any list state (short list, full list, scrolled list, with/without banners, with/without fold indicators `▲/▼ more`, with minimal and maximal header length). No render exceeds the pane height and the top line is never scrolled off.

3. **No regression in other modes:** Detail-mode rendering (`formatDetailView` and renderer detail path with pinned header+ToC) and filter-mode rendering are unchanged — existing tests for the pinned ToC (WL-0MSI28AP80002F5S / WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I), `'keeps the ToC pinned at the top while the document scrolls'`, and filter prompt still pass with no behavior change.

4. **Unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`:** Cover (a) header truncation at narrow width — visible length ≤ `cols` and `Work Items` text still present for a long header at 40 cols and 60 cols; (b) line-count invariant (`lines.length <= rows - 1`) for list mode at narrow width (40×24) with a long header, with banner active, and without banner; (c) wide-pane sanity (80×24 / 120×24) still passes — no over-truncation for short headers.

5. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and any relevant README/docs entries describing the header layout (`packages/herdr/README.md`).**

6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Surgical fix in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `createListRenderer` list-mode header path only — do not change detail/filter rendering or the dynamic list/metadata panel layout beyond the header fix.
- Reuse the existing `truncateLine(line, maxWidth)` helper (ANSI-aware) — no new dependencies or truncation implementations.
- Preserve ANSI styling (bold Work Items, dim/colour for status segments) when truncating; the ellipsis `…` must close open ANSI codes via `ANSI.reset` as `truncateLine` already does.
- Must preserve the `rows - 1` invariant from WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO — the fix must not add chrome rows; the header must remain a single chrome row.
- No change to `renderDowntimeStatus` idle timer growth — truncation must remain correct as the `[⏳ downtime idle m:ss]` string grows (regression guard).

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `createListRenderer` (around lines 3217–3229) builds the list-mode header:
  ```ts
  let header = ` ${ANSI.bold}Work Items${ANSI.reset} — ${totalItems} item(s)${filterLabel}`;
  if (totalCount !== undefined && totalCount > totalItems) { header += ` (top ${totalItems} of ${totalCount})`; }
  if (autoRefresh) { header += ` ${ANSI.dim}[auto-refresh on]${ANSI.reset}`; }
  if (panePaused) { header += ` ${ANSI.fg(220)}[paused — hidden]${ANSI.reset}`; }
  if (downtimeStatus) { header += downtimeStatus; }
  output.push(header);
  ```
  The header is pushed without `truncateLine(…, cols)`, unlike banners (`truncateLine(bannerLine, cols)`) and footer/tooltip lines. When `visibleLength(header) > cols`, the pty wraps it onto a second physical row so `output` logically has `rows - 1` lines but physically occupies `rows` or more, scrolling the first line off the top (observed in narrow panes even with minimal `[Downtime Off]` content, and exacerbated by `codeFreezeActive` banners, long `filterLabel` like `(filtered: stage in_review)`, or large `totalCount`).

- Detail view header/ToC is already pinned (WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I / WL-0MSI28AP80002F5S): `formatDetailView` pins `DETAIL_HEADER_LINES + tocLines` at the top and only the body scrolls — not affected by this list-mode header issue.

- Prior fix WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO corrected layout accounting for group separators and notification-line overflow, and WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ accounted for `▲/▼ more` indicators in the `budgetForRows` budget — but neither guarded the header's own width.

- `truncateLine` (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts:1224`) is ANSI-aware and already used for banners; `renderDowntimeStatus` (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts:3077`) returns ANSI-wrapped status strings of varying length.

- No existing tests assert the header's visible length constraint at narrow widths; the overflow only appears visually in the pty and is not caught by current line-count tests which use wide (80/253) cols.

## Desired change

1. In `createListRenderer` list-mode branch (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` ~3220–3233), apply the existing `truncateLine` to the assembled header before pushing it:
   ```ts
   header = truncateLine(header, cols);
   output.push(header);
   ```
   (Keep the existing `output.push` as a single row; do not add a second header row.)

2. Verify the fix maintains the `rows - 1` invariant when the header is long — the header now costs exactly one line regardless of `cols`, so no additional chrome accounting is needed, but the safety clamp at the end of the renderer (`while (output.length > rows - 1) output.pop()`) remains as a backstop.

3. Do not change `renderDowntimeStatus`, `computeDynamicLayout`, `formatDetailView`, or the detail/filter render paths.

4. Update code comments on the header assembly to note the truncation guard and narrow-pane wrap prevention (reference this work item and WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO).

5. Add narrow-pane unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` per AC 4 and ensure all existing tests remain green.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `createListRenderer` list-mode header assembly (`Work Items …` concatenation and `output.push(header)`) and `truncateLine` helper; primary fix location.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Add header truncation and narrow-pane `rows - 1` invariant tests (list mode, with/without banners, varying header lengths); keep existing detail pinned-ToC tests green.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Update if it describes the header/status bar layout; otherwise code-comments only.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO** — "Herdr plugin: selection list header and top lines cut off top of pane" (completed, critical) — introduced the `rows - 1` / `rows` line-count invariant and corrected separator/notification accounting; this item extends the same invariant to the header's own width.
- **WL-0MSI28AP80002F5S** — "Detail view ToC overflows pane — first lines scroll off the top of the screen" (completed) — the detail-view analogue with pinned header+ToC; this list-mode header fix is the list-mode counterpart and must not regress that fix.
- **WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I** — "Detail view ToC for Related Docs" (completed) — introduced the pinned ToC design preserved by the previous item.
- **WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ** — "Herdr selection list: no indication of items below the fold" (completed) — introduced `▲/▼ more` indicators with explicit `budgetForRows - indicatorRows` accounting; relevant to the chrome budget near the header.
- **WL-0MSQ44MDX008U69J** — "Herdr selection list: let list take as much space as it needs; metadata fills the rest and scrolls" (completed) — introduced `computeDynamicLayout` and the `chromeLines = 2 + bannerCount` budget that the header consumes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: Over-truncation hides useful status.** Mitigation: `truncateLine` preserves the leading `Work Items — N item(s)` prefix and only drops trailing status segments; at 40 cols the most informative prefix remains visible and full status is available in wider panes. Document the truncation behavior.
- **Risk: `truncateLine` double-counts ANSI vs display width.** Mitigation: reuse the proven `truncateLine` implementation already used for banners; add a test that asserts visible length (via `stripAnsi`) after truncation, not raw string length.
- **Risk: Growing idle timer (`m:ss`) eventually pushes other segments off.** Mitigation: tested as part of the variable-length `downtimeStatus` combinations; the truncation guard is independent of which status variant is active.
- **Risk: Breaking existing line-count tests that assume header length.** Mitigation: widen the test cols or update expectations to account for truncation — no functional change for 80+ cols where the header already fits.
- **Assumption:** The reported wrap is in **list mode** (the main `Work Items` list), not in detail mode — confirmed by operator (Q4/Q5). If detail-mode header wrapping is later reported, a separate item should cover it.
- **Assumption:** Narrow pane is the primary reproduction (`cols ~ 40–80`); the fix is validated at 40 cols as the lower bound (below 40 the pane is pathological and the existing `while (output.length > rows - 1) output.pop()` backstop applies).
- **Scope creep:** A richer fix could elide individual status segments (e.g. hide `[auto-refresh on]` first, then downtime) instead of raw truncation — explicitly out of scope for this bug; file as a follow-up enhancement if desired.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "When you say 'the info line at the top,' are you referring to the metadata table (Status, Priority, Stage, etc.) that sits below the pinned header in the detail view?" — Answer (user): "I mean the very first line, it contains the Work Items count, the auto-refresh status, the downtime status." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01 — Q&A round 1, Q1. Research: inspected `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `createListRenderer` header assembly (lines 3217–3229); top line is `Work Items — N item(s) [auto-refresh on] [Downtime …]` plus optional filter/paused segments.
- Q: "Should the fix pin the metadata table as well (so only the description/document viewer scrolls), or is there a different line/section you have in mind?" — Answer (user): "No." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01 — Q&A round 1, Q2.
- Q: "How many items should be in scope — just the metadata table in the detail view, or also the list-mode metadata panel at the bottom of the pane?" — Answer (user): "It has nothing to do with the meta-data (see 1)." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01 — Q&A round 1, Q3. Research: confirmed the issue is the list-mode header, not any metadata panel/table; detail view already has a pinned header+ToC via WL-0MSI28AP80002F5S.
- Q: "When this happens, is it the main list header (`Work Items — N item(s)...`) or a different line? And does it happen during normal list mode, or specifically when you're in the detail view for an item?" — Answer (user): "4 main" (i.e. the main list header). Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01 — Q&A round 2, Q4. Research: `createListRenderer` list-mode branch pushes `header` as `output[0]`; detail-mode path returns via `formatDetailView` and never renders the `Work Items` header.
- Q: "Does it happen with narrow terminal windows (e.g., 80 cols), or also at wider widths?" — Answer (user): "5. Narrow." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01 — Q&A round 2, Q5. Research: wide pans (253 cols) have ample space for the header; narrow panes (40–80 cols) reproduce the wrap — banners and long filter labels exacerbate it.
- Q: "Does the downtime status text include a timestamp that grows as time passes (e.g., `[downtime idle m:ss]`) — could this growing timestamp eventually cause the header line to wrap?" — Answer (user): "6. no - happens event when it says `[Downtime Off]`." Source: interactive reply, 2026-09-01 — Q&A round 2, Q6. Research: `renderDowntimeStatus` (worklist.ts:3077) returns `. [Downtime Off]` (shortest variant) when the worker is disabled — wrap reproduces even with this minimal segment, confirming the bug is not timer-growth-specific; discovered a typo in the answer ("event" = "even") and did not alter the captured intent.
data.title: Prevent top line info bar from scrolling off screen

## Problem statement

The system has recurring crashes that are not being reported or reviewed:

- /var/crash/_usr_bin_node.1000.crash - a 616 MB crash dump from Aug 17 (node process)
- 10+ chrome-headless int3 traps in the kernel log across Aug 18-20
- /var/crash/kdump_lock and kexec_cmd exist but no kdump crash dumps are captured (kernel crash handling not generating reports)

Crash dumps are accumulating (616 MB is significant) without review or reporting, meaning recurring crash patterns go unnoticed until they cause a system outage (as happened on 2026-08-20).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Verify whoopsie/apport crash reporting is functional (systemctl status whoopsie, apport status) and report generation is enabled
- [ ] Review the existing /var/crash/_usr_bin_node.1000.crash dump and record what it reveals (what crashed, why) in a comment on this work item; decide whether to keep or purge it (616 MB)
- [ ] Confirm whether kernel crash reporting (kdump/kexec) is configured to capture the next kernel panic; if not, either configure it or document why it is intentionally disabled
- [ ] Ensure crash dumps are rotated/aged so they cannot fill the disk (e.g. whoopsie retention settings or a cleanup job)
- [ ] Document the crash-reporting setup and retention policy in a comment on this work item or docs

## Key files / commands

- /var/crash/, whoopsie/apport config (/etc/default/apport, /etc/whoopsie)
- `apport-cli` / `whoopsie` status, `du -sh /var/crash`
- Discovered from: RCA of system hang 2026-08-20 (session analysis; no parent work item)

# Write unit tests for auto-downgrade of critical priority

## Goal
Add comprehensive unit tests covering the auto-downgrade behavior for critical priority items transitioning to terminal states.

## Test Coverage Required

Per Acceptance Criteria 4 of parent (WL-0MSJM4EIV001A0V9):

1. **`wl update --status completed`** — verify critical priority downgraded to high
2. **`wl update --stage in_review`** — verify critical priority downgraded to high
3. **`wl close`** — verify critical priority downgraded to high
4. **No-op: non-critical priorities** — verify high/medium/low unchanged on terminal transition
5. **No-op: non-terminal transitions** — verify critical priority unchanged when moving between non-terminal stages (e.g., `idea` → `plan_complete`)

## Implementation Notes

- Tests should use the existing test infrastructure (see `tests/database.test.ts` and `tests/cli/`)
- Follow the existing test patterns for `cascadePriorityDowngrade` tests
- Tests should verify both the priority change AND the reporting output (AC3 of parent)
- Consider both JSON and human-readable output paths

### Key Files
- `tests/database.test.ts` — database layer tests
- `tests/cli/` — CLI command tests (update, close)

# Allow bounded concurrent downtime dispatches during cheap mode (use both local slots)

## Problem statement

Proxy usage analysis of the 04:00-06:00 cheap-mode window (2026-08-22 report, `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`) shows the local Qwen3 model busy only ~25-38% of the window. Root cause is structural, not demand: the downtime worker dispatches strictly **single-flight** (one work item at a time, WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY), each dispatched session consumes exactly **one** local slot, and cheap mode provides **two** slots. The second cheap slot is essentially never used, and the per-item tail (agent tool-execution gaps between generation bursts, 10s-5min each) is pure idle that nothing else can fill.

24 herdr `audit-WL-*` sessions ran nearly sequentially: short generation bursts (3-10s) separated by long tool-execution gaps. Inter-run scheduler dead time (60s idle threshold + 10s poll + spawn) added another ~70s per dispatch cycle.

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — pays for remote fallback tokens; wants maximum value from the always-on local iGPU during cheap hours (01:00-10:00).
- **Herdr downtime users** — want more audits/work items completed per night.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. During cheap mode, the downtime worker MAY dispatch a second work item to fill an otherwise-idle second local slot, subject to a bounded concurrency cap (start with 2 concurrent dispatches).
2. Dispatch of the second item respects the same idle-gate contract (requires `requiredFreeSlots` free slots observed for the idle-threshold duration) — it must NOT queue or dispatch into a busy slot.
3. The concurrency cap is configurable via downtime settings (default 1 = current behavior, so fast/operator-interactive mode is unchanged unless explicitly enabled).
4. Fast mode (3 slots) and operator-interactive sessions keep priority: downtime never displaces an active operator session slot; only genuinely free slots are used.
5. Tests: bounded-concurrency dispatch logic (cap honored, second dispatch only fires when ≥1 slot free for N polls), no regression to existing single-flight claim safety (WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY).
6. Measured outcome: nightly cheap-window busy % for the local model increases vs. baseline (target ≥ 2x the current ~25-38%).

## Notes

- Coupling: dispatched audits run `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1`, so ONE audit uses at most 1 slot (parent then child serially). Two concurrent audits therefore use at most 2 slots = exactly cheap mode's capacity (WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS). Raising fan-out (see the AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM item) changes this budget and must be coordinated — total in-flight local streams must not exceed the cheap pool.
- Related: WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG (same-slot idle tracking), WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS (audit fan-out bound), WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY (single-flight dispatch), WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2 (referenced in code comments, not found in worklog — verify against per-slot idle tracker).
- The 04:00-06:00 evidence (24 sessions, 252 local streams, 48% idle stream-level) is in `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md` and the analysis session log.
data.title: Allow bounded concurrent downtime dispatches (use both cheap-mode slots)

data.description:
## Problem statement

Two coupled defects leave valid audits visible as stale ("out of date audit"):

1. **Comment bumps invalidate audits.** `wl comment add` -> `createComment` -> `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt` (packages/shared/src/database.ts:3282, persistent-store `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt` ~3416) advances the work item `updatedAt` for ANY comment. `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` (packages/shared/src/icons.ts:269) compares `auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`; a comment added after the audit (e.g. "Audit re-evaluation (forced --force)" on WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B at 21:26:17Z vs audit 21:21:03Z) therefore flips the audit to stale even though no content changed. The documented guarantee in icons.ts ("Flag-only flips of needsProducerReview do not move updatedAt, so a previously valid audit remains fresh") does NOT cover comments - comments are the common case that breaks it.

2. **Audit persistence does not atomically update auditedAt.** `wl audit-set` (src/commands/audit-result.ts) writes the `audit_results` row (auditedAt = now) but does not touch the work item; `wl update --audit-text` (src/commands/update.ts) also only writes `saveAuditResult`. There is no single atomic operation that both records the audit AND refreshes the freshness clock, so a comment between audit and display (or a re-evaluation that comments instead of persisting - see WL-0MT8KT2LO0056KLF) leaves the record behind `updatedAt`.

Investigation outcome - audit-content comments can be removed (no consumer parses them):
- implement skill: reads the audit **record** (`/skill:audit` -> runner -> `wl audit-show`; `audit_report_<id>.md`); comments are only generic context in Step 4 ("pay attention to comments"), never parsed as verdicts
- ship skill `check-audit-gate.js`: `wl audit-show` -> `readyToClose`/`rawOutput`/`summary`; `wl comment add` is used only to WRITE merge logs
- heartbeat, report skill, herdr TUI (`worklist.ts`, icons): all read `auditResult`/`auditedAt` from the record

So the audit verdict must live in the audit record only; audits duplicated in comments are dead weight and actively harmful (they bump updatedAt).

Discovered-from: WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B.

## Desired change

1. **Freshness clock:** make audit freshness reflect content-only changes. Options to evaluate (pick one, document trade-offs):
   a. exclude comments (and `needsProducerReview` flag flips, already excluded) from `updatedAt` bumps via `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt`; or
   b. `isAuditFresh` uses a content/activity fingerprint rather than `updatedAt`; or
   c. `wl audit-set`/`--audit-text` perform an atomic "record audit + set updatedAt = auditedAt" so a later comment still breaks it (not fully fixing) - likely insufficient alone.
2. **Atomic audit persistence:** `wl audit-set` (and/or `wl update --audit-text`) should be a single operation that records the `audit_results` row and refreshes the item's freshness marker so "audit recorded" always implies "audit fresh" immediately.
3. **Remove audit-content comments:** stop adding the audit report/verdict to work-item comments (the verdict lives in the audit record). Keep comments for dispatches/trails (herdr "Auto-dispatched..." is a dispatch marker, not audit content - out of scope) and for human annotations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After a post-audit comment is added, the audit remains fresh: `wl show <id> --json` + a comment -> `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` stays true; TUI keeps the passed icon, not stale (add a regression test in packages/shared tests for the chosen mechanism)
- [ ] `wl audit-set` is atomic: after it, `auditedAt >= updatedAt` immediately (no intermediate window where a read shows stale) - or the alternative chosen mechanism guarantees the same
- [ ] The audit report/verdict is no longer duplicated into work-item comments by audit flows; existing duplicated comments on WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B are documented as legacy (no migration required unless trivially safe)
- [ ] Unit tests cover: comment-after-audit keeps fresh; audit-then-comment ordering matches the chosen freshness clock; `wl update --audit-text` path behaves identically to `wl audit-set`
- [ ] Docs updated: icons.ts guarantee comment, docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md (or equivalent), audit SKILL.md where it describes the audit record as canonical
- [ ] Full project test suite passes

## Key files (predicted)

- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` - `isAuditFresh`, `stageDisplayIcon` (the stale-passed path)
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` - `createComment`/`touchWorkItemUpdatedAt` (~3246, 3416)
- `src/commands/audit-result.ts` - `wl audit-set` (atomic auditedAt write)
- `src/commands/update.ts` - `--audit-text` persistence path
- `src/commands/comment.ts` / `packages/shared/src/database.ts` - comment updatedAt semantics
- `packages/shared/src/icons.test.ts` (or equivalent) - freshness regression tests

## Related work

- WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B - observed stale audit (discovered-from)
- WL-0MT8KSTOE00871E7 - herdr interim freshness re-check (sibling)
- WL-0MT8KT2LO0056KLF - forced re-evaluation must persist (sibling; comment-only re-eval is the trigger that exposed this)
- WL-0MSN6ZCTN0027U2R - flag-only flips do not move updatedAt (docs this gap for the needsProducerReview case)
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSN7XAUS008WOPQ** - audit runner: 'Yes' verdict with fallback-tainted ACs silently restores state instead of advancing to in_review (completed)
- **WL-0ML8KC4J11G96F2N** - Dialog State & Single db.update Submission (M4) (completed)
- **WL-0MRJ3TUPP002TSGI** - Change in_review icons and reuse audit column for requiresProducerReview flag (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` - matched: 0msn6zctn0027u2r, 60s, acceptance, actively, activity (+183 more)
- `CLI.md` - matched: actively, add, added, adding, already (+138 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` - matched: 03z, 0msn6zctn0027u2r, 0mt3flzj20076x9b, 60s, actively (+124 more)

## Plan

Child work items created:

1. **Test: comment-after-audit keeps freshness** (WL-0MTHRSZJK008ATDB) - regression test
2. **Fix: atomic audit persistence updates updatedAt** (WL-0MTHRW3770014H51) - core fix
3. **Remove audit-content comments from audit flows** (WL-0MTHRX6YY00891ST) - remove harmful comments
4. **Test: audit-then-comment ordering and audit-text path** (WL-0MTHRY9NP004R9MC) - additional tests
5. **Docs: update audit freshness and record documentation** (WL-0MTHRYRU1004GCH8) - documentation

### Design decision: Option (c) - Atomic audit persistence

Chosen approach: `wl audit-set` atomically sets `updatedAt = auditedAt`.

Trade-offs:
- (a) Exclude comments from updatedAt bumps: Would require changes to touchWorkItemUpdatedAt to accept an optional 'skip' parameter. Risk of side effects on other freshness-sensitive features.
- (b) Content fingerprint gate: Already partially implemented in audit_runner (SA-0MSL1Z70C007B9VZ). Provides content-based freshness but does not fix the TUI's time-based `isAuditFresh()` check.
- (c) Atomic persistence: Simplest, most targeted fix. Ensures auditedAt >= updatedAt immediately after audit, so time-based freshness always passes. No changes to comment handling needed.

Selected (c) because:
1. Minimal scope - only changes audit persistence, not comment handling
2. Fixes the root cause (auditedAt < updatedAt race) directly
3. Works with both the TUI's time-based check AND the content fingerprint gate
4. No risk of unintended side effects on comment handling

### Dependencies

- WL-0MTHRSZJK008ATDB depends on WL-0MTHRW3770014H51
- WL-0MTHRY9NP004R9MC depends on WL-0MTHRW3770014H51
- WL-0MTHRYRU1004GCH8 depends on WL-0MTHRW3770014H51 and WL-0MTHRX6YY00891ST

### Existing fixes referenced

- persist_audit.py already fixed to not pass --stage (SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM)
- audit_runner already has content fingerprint freshness gate (SA-0MSL1Z70C007B9VZ)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- Q: Which freshness clock approach to use? Answer (Map): Option (c) - atomic audit persistence. Reason: minimal scope, fixes root cause directly, works with both time-based and fingerprint freshness.
- Q: Should comments be excluded from updatedAt bumps? Answer (Map): No. Option (c) avoids this. Excluding comments is broader and riskier.
- Q: Should audit-content comments be removed? Answer (Map): Yes. No consumer parses them; they only cause harm by bumping updatedAt.

## Problem

The `wl sync` command uses a binary author-identity gate: it either allows ALL commits from the configured user.email or rejects them all. When syncing against a remote with commits from a different author identity (e.g., a different email address), sync fails with a hard error.

This is annoying for single-operator repos with multiple machines/emails (false positives) and does not scale for team or CI scenarios.

## Proposed Solution

Replace the binary allow/deny gate with a configurable **author whitelist** (`syncAllowedAuthors`) in `.worklog/worklog.yaml`:

- **Empty list (default)** - same behavior as now: only accept commits from the local user.email (strictest, no change to current security posture)
- **Non-empty list** - accept commits from any email in the whitelist
- **null or true** - allow any author (current --allow-foreign-author behavior)

### Example config

Empty list (default / most secure):
  syncAllowedAuthors: []

Allow specific additional authors:
  syncAllowedAuthors:
    - sorra@thewizardscode.com
    - alice@company.com

Allow all (explicit opt-in):
  syncAllowedAuthors: null

### Implementation points

1. Add syncAllowedAuthors to worklog config schema (in config.defaults.yaml and validation)
2. Modify the sync author-check logic to read syncAllowedAuthors from config, check commit author email against the list
3. Update --allow-foreign-author CLI flag to set/override the config value
4. Update help text and docs to explain the whitelist model
5. Add tests covering: empty list, non-empty list, null/true, mismatch

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New syncAllowedAuthors config key accepted and validated
- [ ] Default empty list enforces current behavior (only local author)
- [ ] Non-empty whitelist allows commits from listed emails
- [ ] Null/true allows all authors (equivalent to current --allow-foreign-author)
- [ ] --allow-foreign-author flag still works (sets config to null or true)
- [ ] Tests: empty list, non-empty list, null/true, author mismatch rejection
- [ ] Help text explains the whitelist model
- [ ] Existing --allow-foreign-author users are unaffected
data.title: Replace binary author-identity gate with configurable author whitelist

## Goal

Fix the freshness clock so that post-audit comments do not invalidate audits.

## Problem

`wl comment add` calls `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt()` which updates `updatedAt`.
The `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` check in icons.ts returns false when
`auditedAt <= updatedAt - 60s`, so a comment added after the audit makes it
appear stale.

## Proposed solution

Option (c) - atomic audit persistence: `wl audit-set` (and `wl update --audit-text`)
should atomically set `updatedAt = auditedAt` (or `updatedAt >= auditedAt`) when
recording an audit. This ensures that immediately after an audit, the freshness
check always passes, regardless of subsequent comments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl audit-set` sets updatedAt = auditedAt (or later) atomically with the audit record
- [ ] `wl update --audit-text` path behaves identically
- [ ] After audit, `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` returns true immediately
- [ ] No race window where a read between audit-set and display sees stale data

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` - `saveAuditResult` method
- `src/commands/audit-result.ts` - `wl audit-set` command
- `src/commands/update.ts` - `wl update --audit-text` command
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` - `isAuditFresh` function

# Sprint Complete: Auto-Disable Dispatch & Ship Banner

## Problem statement

When all work items in the current sprint have been completed or reviewed (i.e., completed/in_review count >= the browseItemCount setting), the herdr extension should automatically disable downtime dispatching and display a green banner prompting the operator to ship.

## Users

- **Sprint lead / operator**: Sees a clear visual signal when the sprint is done and knows they can ship.
- **Downtime worker**: Stops wasting compute resources dispatching work when there's nothing left to do.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Auto-disable dispatch**: When `completed + in_review` item count >= `browseItemCount` setting, the downtime worker automatically disables dispatching (writes the disable marker, same mechanism as the `d` shortcut).
2. **Green sprint-complete banner**: A green-background, white-text banner replaces the help text below the item list displaying: `Sprint Complete, hit S to ship`.
3. **Re-enable on new items**: When new work items arrive (completed/in_review count drops below `browseItemCount`), the disable marker is removed and the banner disappears, restoring normal behavior.
4. **Banner only when sprint complete**: The sprint-complete banner is shown ONLY when the condition is met AND the help text is enabled (`showHelpText: true`); it does not interfere with code-freeze banners.
5. **All tests pass**: Full project test suite passes with new changes.
6. **Related documentation updated**: Code comments and any relevant docs reflect the new behavior.

## Constraints

- **Fail-closed**: If the item count query fails, default to NOT auto-disabling (conservative).
- **Non-blocking**: The auto-disable must not crash the TUI or block normal operation.
- **Marker reuse**: Use the existing `.herdr-downtime-disabled` marker file mechanism — no new persistence mechanism.
- **Banner placement**: Banner replaces the help text footer area (same chrome row budget accounting as code-freeze banners).

## Existing state

- The `browseItemCount` setting (default 20) controls how many items are displayed.
- The downtime worker already has a disable-marker mechanism (`.herdr-downtime-disabled`) used by the `d` shortcut.
- Code-freeze banners already render above the item list with proper chrome row accounting.
- The help text footer is rendered below the list and is gated by `showHelpText`.
- Completed/in_review items are tracked via `wl list --status completed --stage in_review`.

## Desired change

- Add a completion-check hook that runs on each list refresh and worker tick.
- When the completion condition is met: write the disable marker, suppress the help text footer, and render the green banner.
- When the condition clears: remove the disable marker, restore the help text, and remove the banner.
- The banner text includes "hit S to ship" referencing the existing `S` shortcut for ship confirmation (WL-0MSGG5N5Z0074TLY).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Add completion check logic to the worker tick loop; wire auto-disable into the existing marker mechanism.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Add `sprintComplete` boolean parameter to the renderer; render green banner in place of help text when active.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-disable-marker.ts` — Reuse existing marker write/remove functions; add a `sprintCompleteMarkerExists` check if needed.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — Add `fetchCompletedItemCount()` helper to count completed/in_review items.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — No changes needed (uses existing `browseItemCount`).

## Related work

- Code-freeze banners: `WL-0MSQ0RPQP00636JY` — similar banner rendering pattern.
- Disable marker: `WL-0MT4BWUHW008LIFE` — existing `.herdr-downtime-disabled` mechanism.
- Ship confirmation dialog: `WL-0MSGG5N5Z0074TLY` — the `S` shortcut the banner references.

# Intake Draft — Downtime dispatcher: exclude items needing producer review from selection

**Work item:** WL-0MTIAL65N004T22F

## Problem statement

The herdr downtime dispatcher auto-dispatches the next eligible work item during idle LLM slots, but it currently ignores the `needsProducerReview` flag. Items flagged `needsProducerReview=true` are awaiting a human producer decision and should not be auto-worked; dispatching them wastes local slots, conflicts with the review gate, and can trigger work the producer explicitly paused.

## Users

- **Herdr operators** running `packages/herdr` downtime dispatch in local-model idle periods.
- **Producers** who set `needsProducerReview` to gate an item until human review completes.

User stories:
- "As an operator, I want downtime dispatch to skip items awaiting producer review so idle slots are spent on actionable work."
- "As a producer, I want flagging an item for review to immediately remove it from the downtime queue so it is not auto-started while I review it."

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Downtime dispatch never selects an item with `needsProducerReview === true` as a candidate, across every tier: audit (`completed`/`in_review` without valid audit), implement (`plan_complete` with risk/effort caps), critical-first (critical across stages, including frontier blockers), `intake_complete` → `/skill:plan`, and `idea` → `/skill:intake`. Items with `needsProducerReview === false` or absent/undefined remain dispatchable.
- AC2: The critical-frontier resolver also excludes `needsProducerReview=true` blockers: if the highest-priority critical candidate is blocked only by review-gated blockers (or the critical item itself needs review), the tier returns no candidate and falls through to the next tier.
- AC3: Coordination (leader) path is equally gated: the leader's per-entry fetch/classification (`fetchItem` + tier mapping) skips entries whose current item has `needsProducerReview === true`; the offer list retains the entry for later re-offer after the flag is cleared, and dispatch falls through to the next dispatchable entry.
- AC4: Filtering is fail-safe at every boundary: a missing/unparseable `needsProducerReview` field is treated as `false` (dispatchable); a malformed item never crashes dispatch and never disables a tier.
- AC5: Regression tests cover the exclusion per tier (unit + `downtime-worker`/`index` level) and verify that clearing the flag makes the item dispatchable again; existing herdr and project test suites pass.
- AC6: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- AC7: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Change is confined to the dispatch selection path; do not change the meaning of `needsProducerReview` elsewhere (TUI filters, `wl list --needs-producer-review`, status lifecycle remain unchanged).
- Fail-closed/fail-safe per tier: a filtering error must not crash the worker and must not silently disable an entire tier; follow the existing `DowntimeNextResult` / null-fallback error channels.
- Do not introduce a new `wl next` CLI flag if client-side filtering in the downtime deps suffices and keeps the change minimal; if a server-side filter is added, it must remain backward compatible.
- Preserve existing dispatched-marker, code-freeze, audit-freshness, and active-audit single-flight guards.

## Existing state

- Dispatcher tiers in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` + `packages/herdr/src/index.ts: createDowntimeDeps()`:
  - `getNextAuditCandidate` → `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only` → `selectAuditCandidate`
  - `getNextImplementCandidate` → `wl next --stage plan_complete --risk medium --effort medium -n 10` → `selectImplementCandidate`
  - `getNextItem('intake_complete'/'idea')` → `wl next --stage <stage> -n 10` → `selectNextCandidate` (with plan/intake dispatched-marker change-guard)
  - `getNextCriticalCandidate` → `wl list --priority critical --status open -n 10` → `selectCriticalCandidate` + `resolveDependencyFrontier`
  - Leader coordination path: `dispatchFromCoordination` iterates the durable offer list, `fetchItem` (`wl show` enriched) per entry, tier classification, shared `recordDispatch`/`spawnAgentPane` path.
- None of these filters currently check `needsProducerReview`; `wl list`/`wl next` server-side can filter by `needsProducerReview` (persistent-store `AND workitems.needsProducerReview = ?`) but the downtime deps do not pass it. Client-side `WorkItem.needsProducerReview` is available on every fetched item (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts: normalizeItem`).
- `needsProducerReview` is a tri-state integer → boolean (0/1, default 0) stored in `workitems` and surfaced via `wl list --needs-producer-review`.

## Desired change

- Filter `needsProducerReview === true` items out of every downtime selection path, client-side in the downtime deps (and, if justified, server-side via `--needs-producer-review false` on the `wl` queries):
  - `getNextAuditCandidate`, `getNextImplementCandidate`, `getNextItem`, `getNextCriticalCandidate` exclude review-gated candidates before `select*` (and re-check frontier blockers for critical).
  - Coordination leader path: `fetchItem` result with `needsProducerReview true` is skipped (not a dispatchable tier match) and the loop continues to the next offer entry.
- Treat `needsProducerReview` absent/null as dispatchable (explicit `=== true` check only).
- Add/extend tests in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` and `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` (and `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` for the leader path) covering: per-tier exclusion, frontier exclusion, leader skip, and flag-clear → dispatchable.
- Update downtime-worker header comment and inline tier comments to document the review-gate exclusion.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `createDowntimeDeps`: `getNextItem`, `getNextAuditCandidate`, `getNextImplementCandidate`, `getNextCriticalCandidate`, `fetchItem` wiring; where `needsProducerReview` filtering is added.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — tier orchestration (`dispatchDowntimeWork`, `dispatchFromCoordination`), header contract, per-tier selection helpers; docs + leader-loop handling.
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.ts` — leader dispatch loop iterating the offer list (if separate from downtime-worker; otherwise within `downtime-worker.ts`).
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` / `src/persistent-store.ts` — server-side `needsProducerReview` filter (`AND workitems.needsProducerReview = ?`) if a CLI flag is passed through.
- `src/commands/next.ts` / `src/commands/list.ts` — `wl` CLI surface for `--needs-producer-review` if server-side filtering is used.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `WorkItem.needsProducerReview` normalization (already present; verify shape used by filters).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — regression tests for the new gate.

## Related work

- WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG — audit tier (completed/in_review without valid audit) — dispatch tier filtered here.
- WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6 — implement tier end-to-end (plan_complete risk/effort caps) — dispatch tier filtered here.
- WL-0MT3FM8VA005XBHE — critical items always progress first regardless of stage — critical-first tier + frontier resolver filtered here.
- WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY — dispatched-marker exclusion in audit-tier selection — existing selection-exclusion pattern this change follows.
- WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT — downtime dispatched-marker change-guard (RCA) — existing plan/intake exclusion pattern.
- WL-0MLGTWT4S1X4HDD9 / WL-0MLGTKW490NJTOAB — `--needs-producer-review` filter and Needs Producer Review flag — storage/query capability reused.
- WL-0MSN6Z9HN00637XY — flipping needsProducerReview must not make a valid audit stale — adjacent invariant to preserve.
- WL-0MTEZ4XZJ006Y9U7 / WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL — coordination (leader offer list) path — leader per-entry classification filtered here.

Automated find_related report: see `find_related` step output persisted to `.worklog/tmp/` (if generated).

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: `needsProducerReview === true` means "human must act first — do not auto-dispatch for any skill (audit/implement/plan/intake)". If some tier should still dispatch (e.g. audit while awaiting review), that would need a separate follow-up item — ask rather than expanding scope.
- Assumption: filtering is `=== true` only; absent/false/undefined items are dispatchable. No tri-state "unknown = blocked" interpretation.
- Assumption: when every candidate in a tier needs review, the tier reports "no candidate" (not a `wl-error` strike) and dispatch falls through exactly as an empty backlog does — no cooldown triggered.
- Risk: adding filtering at both server and client layers could double-filter or mask errors; prefer client-side filtering first and add server-side flag only if it eliminates a meaningful batch-starvation window (batch is already `-n 10`).
- Risk: leader offer list could starve if every offered entry needs review — the leader must fall through gracefully and not pause with a no-candidate cooldown while review-gated items exist.
- Scope-creep risk: extending the flag's semantics (e.g., auto-clearing on review, new `wl next --needs-producer-review` default) is out of scope — record as separate work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should downtime dispatch skip items needing producer review? — Answer (operator): Yes — "When the downtime dispatcher selecting next issues to work on do not select work items marked as needing producer review." Source: intake seed text (`/intake` argument).
- Q: Which tiers does this apply to? — Answer (assumption documented, no question asked): All dispatch tiers (audit, implement, critical-first, plan, intake) and the coordination leader path. Reasonable default: review-gated items should not be auto-worked at any tier. Source: inferred from seed ("selecting next issues to work on" = all selection).
- Q: How does a flagged item become dispatchable again? — Answer (assumption documented, no question asked): Clearing the flag (`wl update <id> --needs-producer-review false`) makes it eligible again; the next idle poll may then select it. Source: existing flag semantics, no change to lifecycle.
data.title: Downtime dispatcher: exclude items needing producer review from selection
